description: Convolution: every output cell is a weighted sum over a small window of the input, the same kernel slid over every position.

line_docs: The whole output map at once: window the input, multiply every window by the kernel, sum the three window axes away by name.
m.purpose: Read right to left: ⧉[Mw,Nw] X gathers every sliding window of the input at once, W × multiplies each window by the kernel (the kernel broadcasts against the stack of windows), +/[channel,kernel_y,kernel_x] sums the three named axes away in one pass, Y receives the whole output map. No index appears. Placeholder glyphs.
m.title: The same layer as sw-MLPL says it

line_docs: Output cell (r, x, y): over every channel q and every kernel cell (u, v), multiply the weight by the input entry the kernel cell sits on, and add all those products up.
math.purpose: One line, three nested sums: for output filter r at position (x, y), sum over the input channels q and the kernel offsets u, v the weight W[r,q,u,v] times the input entry X[q, x+u, y+v]. Every bound is a dimension of one of the two arrays.
math.title: The layer as the paper writes it

name: cnn

docs: The output feature map y: one number per output position, per filter.
Open bracket: the indices of an array entry.
Close bracket.
Separates indices.
Which output filter; here there is one.
The output position's row x: where the window's top edge sits in the input.
The output position's column, also written y in the paper: where the window's left edge sits in the input.
Definition: the left side is computed from the right side.
Add up every term: three sums on paper (channels, kernel rows, kernel columns), one reduce over three named axes in the notation.
Which input channel; here there is one.
How many input channels; here 1.
Which row of the kernel window, 1 to Mw; added to the output row to reach the input row.
How many rows the kernel has; here 3.
Which column of the kernel window, 1 to Nw; added to the output column to reach the input column.
How many columns the kernel has; here 3.
Where each sum starts; the paper counts from 1.
The kernel (the filter's weights): a small grid slid over the whole input, the same at every position. Here a 3×3 vertical-edge detector.
Multiply a weight by the input entry under it; · on paper, × in the notation, where the kernel meets every window at once.
The input feature map: here one channel, a 6×6 grid with a vertical edge in it. X[q, x+u, y+v] is the entry under kernel cell (u, v) when the window sits at (x, y).
Add the kernel offset to the output position to find the input entry under it: this index arithmetic is what the window glyph replaces.
⧉: every sliding window of the input as one array (sw-MLPL's windows); the receptive fields, with no index arithmetic.
The axes the reduce sums away, by name rather than position: channel, kernel-y, kernel-x (sw-MLPL spells them kernel_y and kernel_x; the renderer would read an underscore as a subscript).

title: CNN triple sum

visual.purpose: The input as a grid with the current 3×3 window outlined, the kernel, the nine products of this window as bars, and the output grid filling in one cell per step; the finished cells keep their bars.
visual.title: The window sliding, the products, the output filling in
